I would not choose the Silva direction yet, but I also would not default to the safer lab path. The decision should turn on two gates, not on which story feels more exciting or safer.

First, test whether Silva can become a dissertation: usable data you can access soon, a collaborator deep enough to offset your lab's lack of single-cell experience, and explicit advisor support. A hot field plus uncertain data is not a plan.

Second, protect the fallback while you test Silva. It is only real if it remains advisor-backed, resourced, technically ready, identity-coherent, and protected by a stop-loss date. Give the Silva probe a short, dated window and decide in advance what evidence makes you continue or stop.

The sequence is advisor first, low-cost Silva reality check second, committee only after you know whether the data path is real. Do not go around your advisor with a finished proposal, do not run all options in parallel, and do not treat broad PhD success-rate claims as probabilities for this case. With a three-month deadline and an advisor retiring in 2-3 years, choose only after both executability gates have evidence.

step6_output.answer_core:
I would not choose the Silva direction yet, but I also would not default to the safer lab path. The decision should turn on two gates, not on which story feels more exciting or safer.

First, test whether Silva can become a dissertation: usable data you can access soon, a collaborator deep enough to offset your lab's lack of single-cell experience, and explicit advisor support. A hot field plus uncertain data is not a plan. Treat this as a bounded probe—give it a short, dated window with visible conditions for stopping, not a hidden commitment that becomes hard to reverse.

Second, protect the fallback while you test Silva. It is only real if it remains advisor-backed, resourced, technically ready, and operationally continuous—not just psychologically comforting. Set a clear stop-loss date and decide in advance what evidence makes you continue or stop. Do not rely on broad PhD success-rate claims as calibrated probabilities for your specific case.

The sequence is advisor first, low-cost Silva reality check second, committee only after you know whether the data path is real. Do not go around your advisor with a finished proposal, do not run all options in parallel, and do not let the probe become an implicit dissertation choice. With a three-month deadline and an advisor retiring in 2-3 years, choose only after both executability gates have evidence.
